articles.standfirst: Amanda Mathewson was caught neglecting children at her home in Dunfermline after being spied on by parents.

gist: A childminder who left over 20 children unattended was jailed for two years.
Suspicious parents discovered the neglect after watching her leave for a school run.
An internal probe revealed she was likely tipped off about previous inspections.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Amanda Mathewson, a childminder in Dunfermline, was jailed for two years after pleading guilty to wilfully neglecting and abandoning children. Suspicious parents watched her leave for a school run and found over 20 unattended children inside her home in August 2024. Children were found unsupervised, distressed, and in hot rooms without food or water.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The case exposed a gross abuse of trust and severe regulatory failings. The Care Inspectorate admitted Mathewson was likely tipped off about inspections by an insider, compromising regulatory scrutiny and leading families to explore civil action.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: A learning review by the Fife child protection committee will examine potential improvements to practice and processes. The Scottish government is working with independent regulators to enhance transparency, while lawyers represent families exploring a civil case.

fivew: A childminder was jailed for two years for leaving more than 20 children alone and unsupervised.
She pleaded guilty to wilfully neglecting, abandoning and exposing children to unnecessary suffering.
